documents.unit: Library research guide, section by Center for Educational Effectiveness
documents.title: Generative AI for Teaching, Research and Learning: Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: A guidance page by the Center for Educational Effectiveness inside a library guide. It tells students to check each instructor's policy, gives five takeaways for students, and points instructors to consultations and example syllabus language. It sets no university-wide rule.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own: it says "policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor" and tells students to "check with their instructors", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: CEE experts "are available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies"; this is faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies pertaining to Generative AI
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on all codes (P63, admin, before-course, informs); only topics differed. Source: experts 'are available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies', which is support for policy design. Kept A's topics.

units.why: Says tools 'can be quite useful for personalizing learning experiences and rethinking teaching and instruction', naming a benefit without a rule, so P87 rather than P44; it informs and does not recommend use.
units.anchor: quite useful for personalizing learning experiences and rethinking teaching and instruction
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P87, all, general, informs. unit_stance: A neutral, B encourage. The sentence names a benefit as rationale and does not recommend use, so neutral.

units.why: "both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices" asks all users to stay informed; P102.
units.anchor: both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P102, all, general, should). 'both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices' is a duty to stay informed.

units.why: Students 'should always check with their instructors' about course policy before using AI. P78 (learn the course's rules) fits better than P10 since it is not framed as 'when unsure'.
units.anchor: students should always check with their instructors to understand their particular course policies
units.frag_start: Before using Generative AI to support
units.fit_note: Also implies ask-before-use (P10), but the text is unconditional rather than 'when unsure'.
units.resolution_why: A coded P10 (ask first) and before-course; B coded P78 and course-start. Source: 'Before using Generative AI to support their learning, students should always check with their instructors to understand their particular course policies and requirements'. The check is unconditional and aims at learning the course's policies, so P78 rather than P10 (asking when unsure); the student is learning expectations, so course-start, not course design (before-course).

units.why: "Policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor" says the rule is set per instructor; P04 fits.
units.anchor: policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P04, student, informs. Phase: A general, B course-start. Source: 'Keep in mind that policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor' is a fact about how policy is set, not an expectation communicated at course start, so general.

units.why: "Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking" says AI must not replace the student's thinking; P32 fits better than P12 because it is about the student staying the thinker.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P32, student, during-work, should, permit); only topic order differed. 'Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking' keeps the student as the thinker.

units.why: 'Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools' asks students to stay aware of risks without naming any or telling them to verify output, so neither P31 nor P53 fits; UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools
units.uncovered_note: Students are told generally to stay mindful of AI risks and limitations without naming any specific risk. (Coder A had placed it under P31 with the note that it asks for mindfulness of risks and limitations generally, not explicitly for verifying output.)
units.resolution_why: A coded P31 (verify output) and during-work; B coded UNCOVERED and general. Source names no risk and does not say to check or verify output, so P31 would be a stretched fit; UNCOVERED per codebook. It is a general awareness duty, not tied to a work phase, so general. A's fit note (not explicitly verifying) is merged into the uncovered note.

units.why: "Engage with Generative AI output critically" asks students to evaluate output, which is P31.
units.anchor: Engage with Generative AI output critically and practice information literacy
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P31, student, during-work, should). 'Engage with Generative AI output critically' asks students to evaluate output.

units.why: 'Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies regarding Generative AI' binds students to existing integrity and course rules; closest is P78 (follow the course's rules), not P36 because no misconduct classification is stated.
units.anchor: Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies regarding Generative AI
units.fit_note: Also points to academic integrity guidelines generally, which P78 does not name.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P78, student, should. Phase: A general, B during-work. The sentence is a takeaway about conduct while using AI, so during-work. Kept B's topics and fit note since the sentence also points to academic integrity guidelines generally.

units.why: "Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use" asks students to cite AI use, which is P24.
units.anchor: Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P24, student, during-work, should, disclosure-citation).

units.why: The guide says AI "has disrupted established teaching strategies" and raises open questions about protecting learning; it states no rule, so UNCOVERED rather than a stretched fit.
units.anchor: Generative AI has disrupted established teaching strategies for many instructors
units.uncovered_note: Acknowledges that AI has disrupted teaching and raised open questions about how to support and protect student learning, without a rule or stated mechanism.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on UNCOVERED, instructor, general, informs. Source frames disruption and 'ongoing questions about how to support and protect student learning' without a rule or mechanism. Merged uncovered notes.

units.why: "scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications" says evidence on AI and learning is thin; P55 is nearest.
units.anchor: scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications of Generative AI
units.fit_note: States that evidence is still emerging rather than collecting or citing it.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P55, all, over-time, informs; topics merged. Source: 'scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications of Generative AI' says evidence is limited; kept the shared fit note.

units.why: CEE 'provides a number of resources, events, and consultations related to Generative AI and teaching', which is faculty support (P63), stated as a fact about the center, so phase general and modality informs.
units.anchor: provides a number of resources, events, and consultations related to Generative AI and teaching
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P63, actor and modality. Phase: A general, B before-course. The sentence is a fact about what the center offers, not specifically course-policy set-up, so general.

units.why: Says institutions 'developed preliminary guidance for instructors to develop transparent expectations and policies', pointing to syllabus examples; closest to P09.
units.anchor: preliminary guidance for instructors to develop transparent expectations and policies regarding Generative AI
units.fit_note: Recommends transparent expectations by pointing to examples; it does not require a syllabus statement.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P09, instructor, before-course, informs); anchors differed slightly. Kept B's anchor, which names the guidance itself, and B's fit note.

units.why: "Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI into their course materials" encourages instructors to use AI in teaching; P59 is nearest.
units.anchor: Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI into their course materials
units.fit_note: Concerns incorporating AI into course materials and instructional strategies, not only drafting teaching documents.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all codes (P59, may, encourage); merged both fit notes. Source: 'Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI into their course materials and/or instructional strategies'.

units.why: Early scholarship is cited as suggesting "intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning", citing evidence (P55) and favoring critical use.
units.anchor: intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning
units.fit_note: Cites emerging scholarship rather than describing evidence collection.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P55, all, over-time (A) vs general (B), informs, encourage. Source: 'As academic research ... continues to evolve, early scholarship ... has suggested that intentional and critical use ... can support student learning'; evidence still evolving, matching the previous unit, so over-time (A's phase).

notes: Only one included document, a library-guide page by CEE, mostly link lists; the Code of Academic Conduct and IET pages were not fetched (Cloudflare block), so the university layer is thin. Reconciled from coders A and B (16 units each, all matched).
